extracted.intended_audience: authors, peer reviewers, editors, and journal staff working in biomedical/medical journals
extracted.subtask_description: High-level recommendations and standards from the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors covering roles, responsibilities, editorial and publishing issues, manuscript preparation/submission, and use of AI in medical journal publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains the purpose of the ICMJE Recommendations for conduct, reporting, editing and publication of scholarly work in medical journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No detailed guidance on this archive/index page; consult the full ICMJE Recommendations document for the specific purpose and scope statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Should Use the Recommendations?
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifies the intended users of the Recommendations (e.g., authors, editors, journals, reviewers, institutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No detailed guidance on this archive/index page; consult the full Recommendations for explicit user guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: History of the Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides historical context and evolution of the ICMJE Recommendations over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No procedural or evaluative detail on this page; see the full document for change history and implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining the Role of Authors and Contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets standards for who qualifies as an author or contributor and outlines their responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No detailed criteria are present on this index page; consult full Recommendations for authorship criteria, contributor roles, and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Financial and Non-Financial Relationships and Activities, and Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires disclosure of relevant financial and non-financial relationships, activities, and potential conflicts of interest by authors, reviewers, and editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail not included on this page; see full text for what must be disclosed, timing, and forms/processes (e.g., ICMJE disclosure form).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities in the Submission and Peer-Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlines responsibilities of authors, reviewers, and editors during submission and peer review (e.g., timeliness, confidentiality, objectivity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No granular guidance here; full Recommendations contain responsibilities and expected behaviors during submission and peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal Owners and Editorial Freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses the relationship between journal owners and editorial independence, protecting editorial decision-making from inappropriate influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full guidance (examples, policies to safeguard editorial freedom) is in the main Recommendations; not present on this archive page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Research Participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies protections for human research participants, including informed consent and ethical oversight requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the full Recommendations for specific requirements (ethics committee approval, consent language, privacy protections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and Version Control
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how journals should handle corrections, retractions, errata, and version control for published material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This index page lists the topic only; refer to the full Recommendations for policies and examples of corrections and version handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for identifying, reporting, and responding to allegations of scientific misconduct (e.g., fabrication, falsification, plagiarism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed procedures and responsibilities for addressing misconduct are in the full Recommendations; not provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses copyright considerations for submitted and published works, including ownership and licensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See full Recommendations for policies on copyright transfer, licenses (e.g., open access), and related requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlapping Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies on redundant, duplicate, or overlapping publications and how journals should handle them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full text contains definitions, examples (e.g., salami slicing), and guidance for authors and editors; not detailed here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for correspondence sections (letters to the editor), responses, and post-publication discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult full Recommendations for limits, screening, and editorial handling of correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on fees charged to authors or readers (e.g., publication fees, page charges, APCs) and transparency about fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed policies and recommended disclosures are in the full document; not present on this index page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplements, Theme Issues, and Special Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for handling sponsored supplements, themed issues, and special series to preserve editorial independence and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the full Recommendations for requirements on sponsor involvement, disclosure, and labeling of supplements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorships and Partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on sponsorships and partnerships involving journals, including disclosure and management of sponsor influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full guidance (e.g., acceptable sponsor roles, disclosure requirements) available in the main Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles and best practices specific to electronic publishing, including online content management and archiving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See full Recommendations for technical and policy details (archiving, DOIs, online corrections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies governing advertising in journals and separation between advertising and editorial content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed advice to maintain editorial independence and transparency about advertising is in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals and the Media
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for interactions between journals/authors and the media, including press releases and public communication of findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Recommendations include recommended practices for accurate reporting and embargoes; not provided here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards relating to clinical trial reporting, including trial registration, CONSORT adherence, and reporting of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the full Recommendations for specific trial registration requirements, reporting standards, and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing a Manuscript for Submission to a Medical Journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions and standards for manuscript preparation (structure, reporting guidelines, ethical statements, formatting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed requirements (e.g., structured abstracts, word limits, reporting checklists) are in the full Recommendations; not included on this index page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sending the Manuscript to the Journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural guidance for submitting manuscripts to journals (cover letters, submission declarations, required documents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See full Recommendations for required submission materials, declarations, and recommended processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI by Authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on authors' use of artificial intelligence tools in preparing manuscripts, including disclosure and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full Recommendations provide specifics on what should be disclosed and how AI use affects authorship and responsibility; not detailed here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI by Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on reviewers' use of AI tools during peer review, including confidentiality and proper use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the full Recommendations for explicit reviewer obligations and limits when employing AI tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors' Role in Ensuring Responsible Use of AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for editors to set policies and ensure responsible use of AI across authorship and peer review processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed editorial policies and recommended workflows regarding AI are in the full Recommendations; not present on this index page.
